fixes.explanation: That's it. The psalm says the LORD redeemed them "…from the hand of the enemy" (Psalm 107:2). Redeemed is the word the psalm uses for them. Anybody who's come through a tough spot can lift a hand on that one.

That's a picture from another passage, friend, not this one. The fiery furnace is in Daniel 3:20. Verse 2 here says He redeemed them "…from the hand of the enemy" and there's no furnace anywhere in this psalm. Stay with that enemy's hand, because that's what the redeemed got out of.

Straight, yes. "He led them on a straight path to reach a city where they could live." (Psalm 107:7) Earlier they were finding no path to a city, and now He leads them on a straight one. That's quite a change from wandering the wastelands.

Hidden isn't what the verse says, friend. It says He led them on a straight path to reach a city where they could live. (Psalm 107:7) The wanderers were finding no path, and now He's the one leading them. A straight path, and a city at the end of it.
Lighter chains are still chains, friend. The psalm says He "…broke away their chains." (Psalm 107:14) He doesn't just adjust them. He breaks them away.

Yes. "For He has broken down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron." (Psalm 107:16) Bronze gates and iron bars are about as locked as it gets. And He goes through both. That's the reason given this time for the thanks line in verse 15.

True. "They loathed all food and drew near to the gates of death." (Psalm 107:18) Loathed is a strong word for how they felt about food. I think that tells you how serious things were. It's a heavy moment, and the next verse brings the turn.
Yes, "…the gates of death." (Psalm 107:18) They drew near to it. And the very next verse shows where they turn: they cried out to the LORD (Psalm 107:19).

I get the guess, friend, since gates and temples go together in a lot of minds. But the psalm says they "…drew near to the gates of death." (Psalm 107:18) Drew near, and then in the next verse they cry out and He saves them. That's why the cry in verse 19 matters so much.

That's it. "He sent forth His word and healed them; He rescued them from the Pit." (Psalm 107:20) His word is what He sends, and the healing comes with it. The same verse says He rescued them from the Pit.
Bread isn't what the psalm says, friend. It says, "He sent forth His word and healed them…" (Psalm 107:20) His word is what He sends. The same verse says He rescued them from the Pit.
Yes. "Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and declare His works with rejoicing." (Psalm 107:22) Sacrifices and telling His works go together there. The thanks gets said out loud, and with joy.
Yes, "…His wonders in the deep." (Psalm 107:24) These traders are out on the mighty waters, and they see what the LORD does there. The deep is where those wonders show up. Plenty to look at.

A city came up earlier in the psalm, but not in this verse. The traders "…saw the works of the LORD, and His wonders in the deep." (Psalm 107:24) They're out on the mighty waters, doing trade. The deep is where the wonders are.
No army in this verse, friend. It says, "…He spoke and raised a tempest that lifted the waves of the sea." (Psalm 107:25) A tempest is a big storm. It's the one that lifts the waves.

Yes. "He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed." (Psalm 107:29) From a tempest to a whisper, and the waves go quiet. That's a big change. The next verse says they rejoiced in the silence (Psalm 107:30).

Splitting the sea belongs to a different story, friend. In Exodus 14:21 the waters were divided. In this psalm, "He calmed the storm to a whisper, and the waves of the sea were hushed." (Psalm 107:29) Hushed, not split.

That's it. "Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people and praise Him in the council of the elders." (Psalm 107:32) Both the gathering of the people and the council of the elders are named. The psalm calls for praise out in the open.

True. "He turns a desert into pools of water and a dry land into flowing springs." (Psalm 107:35) Verse 33 says He turns rivers into deserts, and this one goes the other direction. Dry land becomes flowing springs.

It's true, friend. Verse 35 says, "He turns a desert into pools of water and a dry land into flowing springs." The same LORD who turns rivers into deserts in verse 33 does this one too. Dry ground doesn't get the last word here.

Right, it's false. "He blesses them, and they multiply greatly; He does not let their herds diminish." (Psalm 107:38) The people multiply greatly, and He does not let the herds diminish. The blessing covers the herds too.

Yes. "But He lifts the needy from affliction and increases their families like flocks." (Psalm 107:41) The needy get lifted from affliction, and their families increase like flocks. It's a good contrast with the nobles in the verse before.
